transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen, Liam Morgan, Priya Nair, Carlos Reyes, Jules Park, Marta Velasquez, Devon Li

SUMMARY:
Quick sync across IT, Finance, and Security to reconcile planned maintenance windows, budget impacts for Q2 reserved capacity, and outstanding compliance evidence for an upcoming audit. Goal: agree on next steps for maintenance scheduling and ensure KMS rotation + SOC2 evidence are on-track.

TOPICS:
- Q2 maintenance windows and blackout periods
- Reserved capacity billing implications and reforecast
- KMS rotation + key custody (on-prem vs cloud HSM)
- SOC2 evidence gap list and owners
- Procurement timeline for additional GPUs / dedicated capacity

ACTION ITEMS (captured verbally, also in metadata):
- Ava to draft maintenance runbook + send to attendees
- Priya to pull and annotate SOC2 evidence list; call out any missing items
- Liam to reforecast committed instance usage and budget impact
- Devon to confirm downstream infra constraints for maintenance windows

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00:00] Ava: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for jumping on. i think we've got about 45 minutes. quick round robin — can we do updates 2 minutes each?
[00:00:12] Liam: yeah that works, i just wanna flag the Q2 numbers, we've got an uptick in reserved usage, the committed instances line is a little higher than forecasted so i'll share a reforecast later.
[00:00:28] Priya: quick from security, SOC two evidence pull is in progress, but KMS rotation is pending and it depends on whether we go HSM or cloud-kms again — couple of vendors ask for HSM certs which we need to validate.
[00:00:45] Carlos: facilities note, planned datacenter maint on 3/20 might affect network tiering, but i'm waiting on the vendor window.
[00:01:02] Jules: procurement is tracking the PO for extra dedicated nodes, timeline is two to three weeks once legal signs off.
[00:01:18] Marta: legal is reviewing the contracts, mostly standard, a couple of redlines on data processing addendum for private deployments.
[00:01:34] Devon: infra side: VPC peering and routing for the private stack — if we do a 2-hour maintenance window we need to ensure KV cache warmup after restart, otherwise latency spike.
[00:01:50] Ava: great; ok let's go item by item. first, maintenance windows. proposed date 3/20 as Carlos mentioned, 2 hours during off-peak 02:00-04:00 UTC. any blockers?
[00:02:05] Devon: that time looks ok but i need to confirm on-call rotation. also the auto-scaling polices might create a fan-out of cold starts, we should pre-warm critical services.
[00:02:21] Liam: cost question — if we pre-warm, that's extra minutes on dedicated, do we bill that as reserved or on-demand? i need the accounting treatment for Q2 forecast.
[00:02:36] Priya: for security, pre-warm means we must also ensure keys are valid post-rotate. if K M S isn't rotated before the window we could have auth failures.
[00:02:52] Ava: ok action: Priya will confirm KMS rotation timing. Liam will model pre-warm cost into forecast. Devon will outline the warmup playbook.
[00:03:07] Priya: quick clarification, when you say KMS rotation do you mean full key roll or just rekeying material? we have to coordinate with the HSM vendor if we go that route.
[00:03:22] Ava: good point, we should define scope. for this maintenance we prefer a rekey with a gradual rollover, not full immediate key replacement.
[00:03:36] Devon: noted. also KV cache persistence — the runtime supports prefix caching but if nodes restart the cache loses hot tokens, we might see a 200-300ms median increase briefly.
[00:03:52] Liam: 200-300ms is material for SLAs, finance will need to account for potential incident cost credit. is there a fallback to a lower-cost model variant during the warm-up?
[00:04:07] Ava: yes we can route to a smaller model for non-critical routes using routing policies; but product teams will push back, so we need comms.
[00:04:21] Jules: procurement question — if we delay the PO sign-off till after 3/20 maintenance, will lead time slip? vendor said 10 business days once PO is in.
[00:04:36] Marta: legal can expedite DPA sign-off but need a final vendor appendix. i'll loop in vendor counsel.
[00:04:50] Priya: SOC two: we have about 7 evidence items outstanding — change control logs, KMS rotation attestations, and a recent pen test report. i'm compiling a list.
[00:05:04] Ava: can you read out the top three missing so we can assign owners?
[00:05:12] Priya: sure — change control tickets for the runtime deploys (owner: infra), KMS rotation policy doc (owner: security), and updated endpoint access matrix for the private deployment (owner: product ops).
[00:05:28] Devon: infra will own the change control tickets, i'll pull history and attach ticket ids.
[00:05:40] Liam: finance question again — if we sign the reserved capacity now, committed pricing starts immediately, we need to reflect that in Q2. what if we shift start to 4/1? vendor flexibility?
[00:05:56] Jules: vendor said start date is negotiable within a two-week window, i'll confirm.
[00:06:08] Ava: ok let's capture that as a procurement follow-up.
[00:06:18] [silence/typing]
[00:06:35] Carlos: quick note on power at the colo; last month there was a brownout in rack B which caused transient packet loss. vendor said they stabilized, but i'd like to include a hardware health check in the maintenance runbook.
[00:06:51] Devon: good call, add hardware checks and network flaps. we'll include metric thresholds to abort if packet loss > 1% over 5 minutes.
[00:07:07] Priya: about K M S again — are keys stored in cloud KMS or customer-managed HSM? we had mixed notes in the last doc.
[00:07:20] Ava: current plan: primary in cloud KMS with customer-managed HSM for critical root keys. Priya, confirm the documented split and whether it meets compliance.
[00:07:36] Priya: will do. also need to check access logs retention period for audit — we're being asked for 12 months minimum.
[00:07:48] Liam: on billing, if we need additional retention or log storage that's an incremental cost — i'll add an item to the forecast.
[00:07:59] Ava: good. next topic: procurement timeline for extra GPUs/dedicated capacity. Jules?
[00:08:08] Jules: timeline: PO ready 3/09, vendor lead time 10 business days, deploy by end of March if no delays. budget-wise we need finance sign-off by 3/10.
[00:08:22] Liam: ok i can turn around a reforecast by 3/10 but need the detailed SKU list and expected utilization.
[00:08:33] Jules: i'll attach SKU list after call.
[00:08:38] Marta: legal needs to confirm data processing addendum for private nodes, especially regarding customer data residency.
[00:08:49] Ava: i'll put that on the runbook too — a pre-checklist for data residency implications.
[00:08:59] [timestamp jump]
[00:12:10] Devon: i'm flagging a technical deep-dive we should schedule next week with runtime team — the KV cache persistence options and warmup playbook need engineering sign-off. propose 60-minute SE-led session.
[00:12:25] Ava: agree; we'll schedule the SE session. Priya, you should be on that too.
[00:12:35] Priya: yes i'll prep the compliance constraints for that session.
[00:12:45] Liam: also, can the SE session include an SLO impact table so finance can model credit exposure?
[00:12:56] Devon: yes we can produce a simple SLO vs median latency delta table per route.
[00:13:08] Ava: perfect. next, SOC2 evidence — Priya you're pulling items, timeline?
[00:13:16] Priya: i'll have a draft list by 3/09; some items require ticket attachments from infra and product.
[00:13:27] Devon: infra will prioritize attaching logs and deploy tickets.
[00:13:33] [crosstalk] Marta: legal also requested a copy of the vendor contract redlines, i'll share after internal review.
[00:13:45] Ava: good. procurement question — what if vendor can't meet 3/20 maintenance? alternatives?
[00:13:56] Jules: we can push to 3/27 or perform a rolling maintenance across racks to reduce impact.
[00:14:07] Carlos: rolling maintenance increases complexity but reduces blast radius. prefer rolling if vendor window is constrained.
[00:14:19] Ava: ok note options: full-window 3/20, backup 3/27, or rolling ops. Devon to recommend technical feasibility.
[00:14:31] Devon: i'll do a short feasibility doc.
[00:14:38] [pause]
[00:15:02] Liam: small ask on reporting: can we get a cost breakdown of the maintenance (pre-warm vs normal ops) so finance can communicate to execs?
[00:15:13] Ava: yes, Liam i'll work with you and the SEs to produce a delta cost model.
[00:15:23] Priya: another compliance note — we were asked about RBAC changes during maintenance. we should ensure no policy drifts.
[00:15:34] Devon: absolutely, role escalations must be time-boxed and audited. we'll include an RBAC rollback plan.
[00:15:45] Jules: procurement will require the vendor SLA revision showing maintenance windows and support response times.
[00:15:56] Marta: legal needs final contract by 3/09 to hit vendor lead times.
[00:16:06] Ava: let's recap: owners and due dates. (reads action items)
[00:16:20] [00:16:20] Ava: Priya — SOC2 evidence list by 3/09.
[00:16:25] Priya: yes.
[00:16:28] Ava: Liam — reforecast and delta cost model by 3/10.
[00:16:33] Liam: yep.
[00:16:36] Ava: Devon — warmup/feasibility doc + KV cache plan by 3/12.
[00:16:42] Devon: god yes, i'll get it done.
[00:16:46] Ava: Jules — confirm vendor lead time and PO timing by 3/08.
[00:16:51] Jules: i'll confirm.
[00:16:54] Ava: Marta — finalize DPA redlines by 3/09.
[00:16:58] Marta: on it.
[00:17:02] Carlos: i'll add colo hardware checks to the runbook, target 3/08.
[00:17:09] Ava: excellent. any other blockers or risks?
[00:17:14] Devon: risk: if key rotation fails we could have auth failures across private cluster — mitigation: staged roll and smoke test with synthetic traffic.
[00:17:26] Priya: add a rollback key and emergency access playbook.
[00:17:33] Ava: ok add that to the runbook.
[00:17:40] [brief side-discussion about calendar invites and timezones]
[00:20:02] [00:20:02] Priya: small note — audit asked for proof of encryption at rest for backups; do we have a short statement?
[00:20:10] Liam: yes, backups are encrypted with AES-256 by default, but i'll attach the storage provider attestation.
[00:20:18] Marta: legal will include the attestation in the vendor appendix.
[00:20:25] Ava: wrap-up: i'll send the runbook skeleton and the meeting notes. who wants to review before i send?
[00:20:33] Devon: i'll review the tech sections.
[00:20:36] Priya: security will review the compliance sections.
[00:20:40] Liam: finance will review the cost appendix.
[00:20:44] Ava: great, target to send notes and runbook draft by EOD 3/05.
[00:20:50] [00:20:50] Jules: noted.
[00:20:55] Marta: noted.
[00:21:00] Carlos: noted.
[00:21:05] Ava: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with calendar invites for the SE deep-dive and the maintenance window confirmation.
[00:21:15] [meeting ends; remaining time used for quick one-on-ones off-record]

NOTES ON TRANSCRIPTION QUALITY: there are a few misheard acronyms ("K M S" spaced out, "SOC two" spelled out), occasional punctuation dropped; still readable and captures action items and owners.
